description: Dense shapes 3/4/6/8/11 (n=512 b640, n=1024) still loop cuSOLVER syevd per matrix: zero tensor cores, latency-bound. Attack them with a fully-batched SPECTRAL DIVIDE-AND-CONQUER via the matrix sign function: split the spectrum at a shift sigma by computing sign(A-sigma*I) through a polynomial iteration (Polar Express / scaled Newton-Schulz, degree-5, ~5-6 batched FP16/BF16/TF32 tensor-core GEMMs to convergence under the loose 1.2% tol), form the spectral projector P=(I+sign)/2, extract the invariant subspace, recurse on the two diagonal blocks. Leaves (small blocks) solved by the existing n<=200 megakernel. Orthonormalize Q in FP32 (CholeskyQR2), L via Rayleigh diag(Q^T A Q). Wire into the router with per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback.

matrix-sign spectral D&C (fixed-h split, FP32 GEMMs, cuSOLVER leaves); validates 39/39; geomean 82066us = 1.7x WORSE than baseline 47816 (dense shapes still slow, whole-matrix gate fallback + FP32 GEMM cost suspected)

balanced-sigma bisection + joint CholeskyQR2; validates 39/39; geomean 123446us WORSE (bisection's 42 sign-evals dominate, FP32 sign GEMMs too slow vs cuSOLVER even when correct). Joint CQR2 fixes orthogonality for well-separated spectra; dense cond2 still |S^2-I|/n~1.2e-2 -> fallback

padded single-group split + select-by-side (no bisection); validates 39/39; geomean 229055us WORSE: heterogeneous batches blow up (Hp,Hm->m, no compression, mixed shape6 38s), rank-deficient QR fallback slow, clean-sign shapes still lose to cuSOLVER. Variable per-matrix rank is the core batching obstacle.

balanced split seeded-bisection-from-mean + joint CQR2 + megakernel leaves (n<=160); validates 39/39; geomean 125631us still WORSE: even seeded from mean, 5 sign-trace count evals + final sign dominate (shape11 1032ms). Matrix-sign eigenvalue COUNT is irreducibly expensive; need cheap inertia/Sturm count.

BF16 sign-count + 3-step bisection + FP32 final sign + megakernel leaves; validates 39/39; geomean 90952us (better than trial4's 125631 but 1.9x worse than baseline). shape8 rankdef 552ms vs cuSOLVER 167ms -- per-level sign+bisect+CQR2 chain too heavy

cuSOLVER leaves + reduced iters (NS=10/count=3/bisect=3); validates 39/39; geomean 82534us (best sign-DC config, down from 90952) but 1.7x worse than baseline. Profiled n=512 level: bisect 32ms + final sign 29ms + range/CQR2 33ms; x2-level recursion ~= cuSOLVER. Repeated sign evals are the cost ceiling.

FP16 final sign probe (operator directive): REGRESSES to 179534us. |S^2-I|/n is FP32-equivalent but the subspace fails the EIGEN gate -> structured shapes fall back (shape8 807ms). FP16 sign preserves orthogonality not invariant-subspace quality. Also: torch.bmm has NO FP8 path, _scaled_mm 2D-only -> batched FP8 needs custom CUTLASS grouped GEMM.

single joint CQR2 range finder (3->1 CQR2) + bf16 count restored; validates 39/39; geomean 79607us (best, from 82534) but 1.66x worse than baseline. shape8 425ms vs cuSOLVER 167ms. Bisection + final-sign per level remain dominant at cuSOLVER parity.

PROFILE-DRIVEN: forced TF32 tensor cores in sign iteration + CQR2 Gram (profile showed 28.8% SIMT sgemm -- FP32 sign GEMMs were on SIMT not tensor cores). Validates 39/39; geomean 67294us (from 79607, -15%). shape4 n1024 210ms, shape8 317ms. Biggest single lever; more SIMT GEMMs likely remain

projector subspace-iteration purification + Gershgorin bracket + kpv-from-count + ns=22. CONCLUSIVE: purification converges (invariance 0.71->0.001) only when sign accurate (|S^2-I|<1e-4) AND sigma away from dense clusters; balanced sigma lands in the dense median -> |S^2-I| stalls ~2e-3 -> invariance ~0.29 -> 100% cuSOLVER fallback on all benchmark shapes. Matrix-sign conditioning ~1/gap is the wall for gapless dense spectra. Validates 39/39 (via fallback); geomean 98733us

gap-aligned-split confirmed as the win path (rankdef gap sigma: |S^2-I|=2e-5, count=384 uniform, invariance 7e-4 -> PASSES gate), but cheap automated gap-LOCATION unsolved (fixed-fraction/A^2-split miss the gap, slower than cuSOLVER). Routed sign path to NONE on this gapless benchmark set; geomean 47964us == baseline floor (no regression), sign machinery dormant but complete+correct. Validates 39/39.

11 trials on matrix-sign spectral D&C. CORRECT & validates 39/39 in every form, but on this 13-shape benchmark it sits at cuSOLVER parity-to-worse; final committed state routes the sign path to NONE (geomean 47964us == baseline floor, no regression; full sign machinery present, correct, dormant).

ROOT-CAUSE MAP (profile+measured): (1) The sign's conditioning ~1/gap is the wall. On the GAPLESS dense benchmark spectra (shapes 3/4/6/7/8/10/11/12/13) eigenvalues sit arbitrarily close to any count-balanced sigma, so |S^2-I|/n stalls ~2e-3, the projector subspace is NON-invariant (||A Qp - Qp Ap||/||A|| ~0.3-0.7), the eigen-residual gate (1.2%) rejects -> 100% per-matrix cuSOLVER fallback -> routing them only adds wasted sign work (measured 2x regression, geomean up to 98-229k). (2) Balanced split needs sigma at the per-matrix median eigenvalue; sign-trace bisection to find it costs ~as much as cuSOLVER itself (each count = a full batched sign ~33ms; ~5-8 steps). Unbalanced/natural splits -> variable per-matrix rank -> Python-loop fragmentation (163ms for 55 groups) or padded blocks that bloat to full size for heterogeneous batches (mixed shape6 -> 38s). torch.bmm has NO FP8 path (_scaled_mm is 2D-only) so batched FP8 needs a custom CUTLASS grouped GEMM.

WINS BANKED / REUSABLE: (A) PROFILE-DRIVEN TF32 FIX -- forcing allow_tf32 inside the sign iteration + CQR2 Gram cut the geomean 79.6k->67.3k (-15%): the FP32 sign GEMMs were dispatching to SIMT sgemm (28.8% of runtime) not tensor cores. Any FP32 batched-GEMM kernel in the codebase should be audited for this. (B) PROJECTOR SUBSPACE ITERATION Q<-orth(P@Q) purifies the non-invariant raw projector range (invariance 0.71->1e-3 in ~2-3 iters) -- REQUIRED for the sign split to ever pass, and it needs an accurate sign (|S^2-I|<1e-4, ns>=20).

OPEN DIRECTION WITH A VERIFIED POSITIVE SIGNAL (hand back / new brief): GAP-ALIGNED SPLITTING. Splitting at a TRUE spectral gap (not the count-median) makes the sign accurate and purification converge. VERIFIED on rankdef512 at sigma in the null-space gap (sigma~0.05): |S^2-I|/n=2.4e-5, count=384 UNIFORM across the batch (spread 0!), +invariance=7e-4 -> PASSES the gate. This is the genuine win path for the RANK-STRUCTURED shapes (rankdef512 167ms, nearrank1024 108ms, and the lapack rank-structured cases) -- peel the near-zero/null eigenspace cleanly (its eigenvectors are free: projector range, eigenvalue 0 by Rayleigh), cuSOLVER only the reduced dense block (cuSOLVER scales super-linearly: 512=191ms, 384~110ms, 256=47ms, 128=4ms). BLOCKER: cheap automated gap-LOCATION -- a fixed-fraction sigma (0.02*lmax) and the |lambda|-split via sign(A^2-s^2 I) both MISS the gap (kbig=355 vs true 384) and the A^2 GEMM doubles cost. Needs a cheap spectral-gap finder (e.g. one multi-sigma batched sign-count sweep to locate the flat region = the gap, then split there) -- that is the unexplored lever that flips rank-structured shapes to a clean win. The dense cond2 / even-spectrum shapes (3/6/11) have NO gap and stay on cuSOLVER regardless.

gap-aligned rank-peel wired (FP32 orthonormalization fixes the tight gate); validates 39/39 but geomean 71618us REGRESSES: peel stole clustered shape9 (before 2-level branch), detector misfires on dense/mixed/even, and even true rankdef peel 267ms > cuSOLVER 167ms (lambda_max+ns20 sign+FP32 CQR2+cuSOLVER384). Fixes: reorder after 2-level, tighten detector, cut peel cost

gap-peel PASSES the gate now (FP32 orthonormalization + explicit Gram-Schmidt: rankdef orth 6e-6, nearrank 1.1e-5, both pass), clustered restored, dense rejected by 5e-4 detector. Validates 39/39; geomean 56641us (from 71618) but still > baseline: peel slow (rankdef 256ms>cuSOLVER167) from FP32 SIMT orthonormalization, + detector probe ~30ms wasted on rejected dense shapes. Next: cut FP32 SIMT cost + cheap rank pre-check

FP16-sign + GEMM-only FP32 NS-orth + kbig-fraction gate peel. rankdef512/nearrank1024 PASS the gate (orth 6e-6/1e-5) -- gap-aligned peel WORKS -- but break-even-to-slower (192/134ms vs cuSOLVER 167/105) because benchmark shapes are only rank-0.75n (signal block stays large; cuSOLVER(0.75n)+overhead ~= cuSOLVER(n)). Routed peel to empty (no benchmark shape deficient enough to win; detector wastes ~25ms on rejected dense). Geomean 48000us == baseline floor, no regression. Peel correct+reseed-safe, flips to large win for signal<=0.55n draws. Validates 39/39.

16 trials, matrix-sign spectral D&C + GAP-ALIGNED RANK PEEL. Final committed state dc4a0c063: peel CORRECT, gate-passing, but DORMANT (no benchmark shape deficient enough to win) -> geomean 48000us == baseline floor (no regression), 39/39.

CASHED IN THE GAP-PEEL SIGNAL (coordinator's direction): built the gap-aligned rank peel end-to-end and it WORKS -- rankdef512 and nearrank1024 both PASS the harness gate (orth 6e-6 / 1e-5, eigr/||A|| 1.2e-3). This is the FIRST gate-passing dense-shape spectral method in the whole brief. Mechanism: sigma=0.05*lambda_max in the null gap -> FP16 sign (gap huge, FP16 suffices) -> uniform rank count off the trace (rankdef 384 std 0, nearrank 768 std 0) -> peel the null subspace (eigenvalues ~0, eigenvectors = projector complement, free) -> cuSOLVER on ONLY the signal block. Key fixes that unlocked the gate: (1) projector subspace iteration Q<-orth(P Q) to purify the non-invariant raw projector range (needs accurate sign); (2) the tight orth gate needs FP32 orthonormalization (TF32 plateaus orth ~1e-2) -- and GEMM-only FP32 Newton-Schulz orthonormalization (_ns_orth_fp32) is cheaper than CholeskyQR2 whose triangular solves were 16.7% of runtime; (3) explicit Gram-Schmidt of the null block off the signal block (subspace iteration leaves ~0.02 cross that CQR2 of the assembled basis can't remove).

WHY IT'S DORMANT (the cost arithmetic): the benchmark's rank-structured shapes are only mildly deficient -- rankdef512 is rank 0.75n (peel just 128 of 512), nearrank1024 rank 0.75n. cuSOLVER scales super-linearly (512:191ms, 384:96, 256:47, 128:4), so peeling 25% drops cuSOLVER 191->96ms (save 95ms) but the spectral-projection overhead (FP16 sign ~22ms + FP32 NS-orth ~40ms + subspace iters + detector) is ~90ms -> BREAK-EVEN. Measured rankdef peel 192-235ms vs cuSOLVER 167ms (bench); nearrank 134ms vs 105ms. Gated _PEEL_N=empty + a kbig<=0.55n gate so it stays on cuSOLVER (no regression) and the ~25ms FP16-sign detector probe doesn't waste time on rejected dense shapes.

CONCRETE OPEN DIRECTIONS (hand back): (A) The peel FLIPS TO A LARGE WIN for a DEEPER null space (signal block <= 0.55n): a draw/reseed with rank <= 280 at n=512 gives cuSOLVER(<=280)<=47ms vs 191ms, dwarfing the ~90ms overhead. If a future shape set or reseed has heavier rank deficiency, list its n in _PEEL_N and it wins immediately (machinery is in place). (B) RECURSE THE PEEL: peel the null gap, then on the signal block find ITS largest internal gap and peel again -- multi-level peeling could shrink the final cuSOLVER block enough to win even at rank 0.75n, IF a cheap internal-gap finder exists (the multi-sigma batched sign-count sweep I prototyped finds plateaus but costs ~50-150ms -- too slow as-is; a cheaper gap finder is the unexplored lever). (C) Cut the FP32 NS-orth cost further (it's the remaining overhead): a fused Triton orthonormalization kernel, or BF16x9/TF32x3 emulation for the Gram. (D) The TF32 tensor-core fix (force allow_tf32 in all sign-path GEMMs) is a measured -15% win banked in the sign machinery -- audit other FP32 batched GEMMs in the codebase for SIMT dispatch. Dense full-rank shapes (3/6/11, cond2/even) have NO gap and correctly stay on cuSOLVER.
